clue.text: Immature parasite, I frolic madly in seas

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, splitting the outer word

parts.note: maria is the plural of mare, a sea, as in the lunar seas

indicators.note: acting madly means behaving wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A young parasite gleefully romps about in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters go between the first M and the rest of MARIA. Maria (Latin seas) is the name given to the dark plains on the Moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A microfilaria is the larval stage of a filarial worm, a parasite found in blood.

clue.text: Address gender-inappropriately, church say mistakenly

parts.note: to refer to someone with the wrong pronoun, playfully coined as a verb
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone misgenders a person and then has the church explain it was an error.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is a playful coinage: to misgender is to use the wrong pronoun, so to 'mispronoun' someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To mispronounce a word is to utter it wrongly, the sounds coming out incorrectly.

clue.text: Excited elation with quail's ensnarement

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so the letters get jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, 'with' joining it to the other word

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled at having trapped a quail.
explanation.definitionFit: Illaqueation, from Latin laqueus, a noose, is the act of catching in a snare.

clue.text: Skin ulcer turning up somewhere in Rajasthan — not the first

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the letters from bottom to top
the opening letter of the place is dropped, as 'not the first' says

parts.note: Jaipur is the capital of the Indian state of Rajasthan

explanation.surface: A skin sore appears on a traveller somewhere in Rajasthan.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupia is a crusted ulcerous skin eruption, seen in secondary syphilis.

clue.text: Scots property owner, one in eastern Forfar

indicators.note: one placed in something sits inside its letters
the eastern part of a word is its right-hand end, so only the final portion of the town name is kept

parts.note: the eastern half of the town's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Scottish landowner lives in the east of Forfar, a town in Angus.
explanation.walkthrough: Forfar is a Scottish town, which suits the Scots answer; its eastern end is the last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots law a fiar is the owner of the fee simple of a property, as opposed to a life-renter.

clue.text: Put in a border so as to allow for events outside Hungary

indicators.note: the phrase stands outside, wrapping around the country's symbol

parts.note: 'in case' means as a precaution against something happening
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary

explanation.surface: Guarding a frontier in preparation for trouble beyond Hungary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For events' completes the phrase 'in case of events' in the surface; IN CASE wraps around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchase is a variant of enchase, to set a jewel in a surround or frame it with ornament.

clue.text: Old satin finally reduced

indicators.note: something reduced is cut down, here losing its last letter

parts.note: 'at last' means finally

explanation.surface: A worn-out piece of satin has at last been cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Satin finally' looks like a last-letter instruction, but 'Old satin' is the definition and 'finally' stands for a whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlas was the name of a rich satin fabric made in the East, a now archaic textile term.

clue.text: Elevated route span really lacking breadth

indicators.note: lacking breadth means the abbreviation for breadth is taken out

parts.note: a bridge spans a gap
'way' is informal for very or really, as in 'way too much'

explanation.surface: A raised road whose span is really too narrow.
explanation.walkthrough: B for breadth comes off BRIDGE. The Ridgeway is an ancient track along the chalk downs of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridgeway is a road or track running along a ridge, so it is high up.

clue.text: In science he'd engineered non-opening of ripe fruit

indicators.note: engineered means built or contrived anew, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A botanist's lab work produces fruit that will not burst open.
explanation.definitionFit: Indehiscence is the botanical term for fruits like nuts that do not split to release their seeds.

clue.text: Collected arranged mortgage deal

indicators.note: arranged means put into a fresh order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A borrower picks up the home loan they have set up.
explanation.definitionFit: To agglomerate is to gather into a mass or heap, so agglomerated things are gathered together.

clue.text: Revealing bad intention mostly over ring

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will

indicators.note: turned over, the shortened word is read backwards
mostly means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: animus is intention or purpose
a ting is the ringing sound of a bell

explanation.surface: Disclosing a malicious plan that keeps coming back to a ring of conspirators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad intention' reads as one phrase, but bad and intention are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illuminating throws light on a matter, making it clear and informative.

clue.text: Partner's knocked back ball in bowls game

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed backwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: a pal is a partner or friend, with the 's
the jack is the small target ball in lawn bowls

explanation.surface: A bowls player's partner sends the jack back during the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapjack is a simple children's card game in which players slap any jack turned up.

clue.text: Merry because embraced by Scots sweetheart

indicators.note: a word embraced by another is held inside it

parts.note: jo or joe is Scots for a sweetheart, as in Burns's John Anderson, my jo
cos is short for because

explanation.surface: Happy because a Scottish lover is holding you close.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocose means playful and humorous, given to joking, hence cheerful.

clue.text: Courtyard quiet at something like ten

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
taken as written
the letters I and O look like the figures 1 and 0

explanation.surface: A quiet yard at about ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The last piece is visual: written in capitals, IO resembles the number 10.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved open area beside a house, originally a Spanish inner courtyard.

clue.text: Bengal quince's good inside bread roll

indicators.note: the letter for good sits inside the fruit's name

parts.note: the bael is the Bengal quince, an Indian fruit tree
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A quince from Bengal makes a tasty filling for a roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagel is a ring-shaped roll of bread, boiled then baked.

clue.text: Fishing with trawl, reeling loses time

indicators.note: the word loses a letter, which simply drops out

parts.note: tottering means reeling, staggering
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A trawlerman reels in his line and loses track of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reeling' looks like a fishing term in this surface; it is the source word meaning staggering.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a board-and-line fishing tackle, or the otter board on a trawl net; ottering is fishing with it.

clue.text: Casually dismiss drink after coffee

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an informal verb for sending someone away
second meaning: a small glass of liqueur taken to follow coffee

explanation.surface: Waving away the after-dinner liqueur that follows the coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Chasse is both a slang verb to dismiss and short for chasse-café, a spirit chasing coffee.

clue.text: Trough for washing ore stone on slope

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
rake is the slope of a stage or roof

explanation.surface: A sluice for cleaning ore set on a stony slope.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds, abbreviated st.
explanation.definitionFit: A strake is a sloping trough in which crushed ore is washed in mining.

clue.text: Seawards old creek section comes to an end

parts.note: a tide going out runs seawards
goe, also geo or gio, is an Orkney and Shetland word for a narrow creek
s is the abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: Heading seaward, part of an ancient inlet peters out.
explanation.definitionFit: To outgo is to go out, and something that goes out, like a light, ends.

clue.text: Interesting occurrence is featured in record lyric

indicators.note: a word featured in another appears within it

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
taken as written
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A notable event is mentioned on a song's recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Featured in' places the word between the record and the lyric, which together also spell epode, a lyric poem.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is a distinct incident or event in a series of happenings.

clue.text: Women trapped by evangelical test for witchcraft

indicators.note: something trapped by another is enclosed within it

parts.note: sim, short for Simeonite, is a dated term for an evangelical churchman
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Women caught by a zealous preacher are put through a witch trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspected witches were thrown into water to swim: floating was taken as a sign of guilt.

clue.text: Note tune never using a middle string

indicators.note: leaving out each word's middle means keeping only its ends

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A musician plays a melody that avoids the middle string of the instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle string' reads as one musical phrase; 'middle' belongs to the wordplay and 'string' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nete was the name of the highest-pitched string of the ancient Greek lyre.

clue.text: It may be old fish, southern European

definitions.note: an archaic adverb meaning perhaps; 'old' marks it as obsolete

parts.note: Perca is the genus of the perch
S is the abbreviation for southern
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A piece of stale fish, perhaps, from southern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Percase is an obsolete word for perchance or perhaps, i.e. maybe so.

clue.text: The reverse of energy seen in a mature spider

indicators.note: the reverse of something reads it backwards, end to start

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a letter seen in a word sits inside it

parts.note: ripe means mature
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Physics jargon about energy found in a full-grown spider.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes between RI and PE of A RIPE, and then the whole is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Epeira is a former genus name for the garden orb-weaving spiders.

clue.text: Local Persian opera, not half fa-la-la

indicators.note: not half means half of the following word is taken away

parts.note: Parsifal is Wagner's last opera
a nonsense refrain in song; half of it is its first three letters

explanation.surface: A Persian in India sings opera without the full fa-la-la refrain.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of fa-la-la, FAL, comes off the end of the opera's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parsi is an Indian Zoroastrian descended from Persians who settled there, so a local of Persian origin.

clue.text: Method of detection working in search and rescue

indicators.note: one word in another is placed inside its letters

parts.note: SAR is the standard abbreviation for search and rescue
on means working, as a machine switched on

explanation.surface: A detection system working during a search-and-rescue mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonar locates underwater objects by sending sound pulses and timing the echoes.

clue.text: Concern over joining uranium section of waste pipe

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

indicators.note: turned over, the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a part is one's concern or role, as in 'for my part'

explanation.surface: Worry over uranium getting into the drains.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-trap is the U-shaped bend of a drainpipe holding water to block sewer gases.

clue.text: Heaviest regularly seen amphibian

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: The heaviest amphibian commonly observed.
explanation.definitionFit: Evet is an old and dialect form of eft, meaning a newt.

clue.text: Water cock around eastern Asian peninsula

indicators.note: around means wrapped about the other letter, which goes inside

parts.note: the kora is the water cock, an Asian rail-like bird
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A wading bird roams around an eastern Asian coastline.
explanation.definitionFit: Korea occupies a peninsula projecting from mainland East Asia.

clue.text: Agree to putting cooker in sale by auction

indicators.note: the appliance put in the sale means it goes inside that word

parts.note: cant is an old and Scots word for an auction sale
an oven is a cooker

explanation.surface: Consenting to put a stove into an auction lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To covenant is to agree formally, entering into a binding contract or promise.

clue.text: Careful thought early on concerns idea evolving

definitions.note: an obsolete word, which 'early on' signals

indicators.note: evolving means developing into a new form, so the letters change order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Thinking hard at the start about how an idea is developing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early on' looks like a first-letter instruction, but it belongs to the definition, marking the word as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Considerance is an old form of consideration, meaning reflection or deliberation.

clue.text: Chased loco optimised to limit resistance

parts.note: a loco, short for locomotive, is a railway engine

indicators.note: to limit something is to bound it, enclosing it on both sides

parts.note: a tuned engine has been adjusted to run at its best
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A pursued locomotive was tuned up to cut its drag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chased' seems to mean pursued, matching the train; it is the metalworking sense of engraved.
explanation.definitionFit: Engine-turned metal is decorated with machine-cut patterns, a form of chasing or engraving.
